To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) butyrate up-regulates COX-2 and (ii) inhibition of COX with a highly selective inhibitor sensitizes human colorectal carcinoma cell expressing COX- 2 protein to the inhibitory effect of the short chain fatty acid, butyrate, on cell growth.

(1) the COX-2 selective NSAID NS-398 enhances the growth inhibiting effect of butyric acid in human colorectal carcinoma cell line HT29 expressing COX-1 and COX-2 proteins, but not in S/KS cell line lacking detectable COx-2 protein and activity; (2) butyric acid up-regulates COX-2 in human colorectal adenoma and carcinoma cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of COX- 2 in colorectal cancer, and the possible use of COX- selective inhibitors to treat this common disease.
the potential for dietary modification to prevent cancer, and the mechanisms underlying the protective effect of dietary fibre and butyrate against colorectal cancer.
the role of dietary fibre and NSAIDs in colorectal carcinogenicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selective inhibition of COX2 activity in colorectal carcinoma cell populations expressing COX- 2 protein may have important therapeutic implications in colorectal cancer prevention and treatment.
COX-2 selective inhibitors may be useful in the treatment and prevention of colorectal carcinoma.
COX-2 inhibition with a highly selective inhibitor, NS-398, enhances the growth inhibiting effects of butyrate only in cells expressing COX protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
butyrate induces COX-2 in human colorectal carcinoma (HT29 and PC/AA/C1 cells) and adenoma cells (PC/AA cells).
the combination of butyrate and COX-2 inhibitors could have potential for the treatment of colorectal carcinoma.
COX-2 selective NSAIDs may be useful as adjuvant therapy in the treatment of colorectal cancer.

the COX-2-selective inhibitor NS-398 enhances the growth inhibiting effect of butyric acid in HT29 cells, but not S/KS cells.
